the_rebase_restoration_is_complete.detail: This was the highest-value item asked and it holds, with one qualification the builder should read. The tracked file sets at 0f65d90 and 99b7942 are identical -- contracts/harness-claims.json, scripts/sovharness/__init__.py and scripts/sovharness/fixtures.py are all present again. The complete tree diff between the two commits is a single path, scripts/sovverify/checks.py, and that difference is a comment re-wrap only: both sides carry the same import of HARNESS_CHECKS and the identical table 'CHECKS = REPOSITORY_CHECKS + HARNESS_CHECKS + PARTICIPANT_CHECKS'. Nothing else went missing. The three declared generated projections (docs/documentation.html, docs/surface.html, .clarity/coverage.json) are not merely regenerated but byte-identical to the pre-rebase candidate, so none of them masks a difference.

the_silent_loss_was_real_and_was_found_i.detail: Recorded because it bears on how much weight a green branch tip carries. At 937f833 the rebase had dropped contracts/harness-claims.json, scripts/sovharness/__init__.py and scripts/sovharness/fixtures.py, and reverted scripts/sov_harness.py to the pre-repair four-kind version carrying the suffix-collision REFERENCE bug -- while scripts/sovverify/harness.py still registered 'sov_harness.py selfcheck' against a module the same commit had deleted. This witness detected it from a file changing under an open read and confirmed it from git ls-tree and the reflog before the coordinator's message arrived. The conflict resolution had taken the pre-repair side on the one commit whose entire content was the repair.

the_grader_refuses_every_defect_this_bra.detail: The central claim, re-proved at 99b7942 with this witness's own fixtures against the real repository tree, not the synthetic tree the shipped selfcheck builds. Control: untouched tree exits 0. Six re-injections, each alone, each exit 1 with the correct kind and no other: PowerShell added to .claude/agents/sov-witness.md frontmatter -> CAPABILITY; 'while the service is accepted but unbuilt' in the sov-proofing description -> VOLATILE; 'while Phase-I boundaries stand' in the sdlc-release description -> VOLATILE; a line citing no_external_effects_in_phase_i in sdlc-release -> RETIRED; console_service_status reverted to OWNER_ACCEPTED_BOUNDARY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED in .claude/workflows/sov-console.js -> STANDING; contracts/nonexistent.json substituted into the CLAUDE.md lookup table -> REFERENCE. None passed unrefused.

the_reference_collision_fix_holds_in_bot.detail: Positive direction: a bogus address stays refused with an untracked file planted at a colliding suffix (archives/old/contracts/nonexistent.json), with one planted deep under a service (services/asset/cache/contracts/...), and -- the sharpest case -- with an untracked file planted at the exact repository-root path the address names. The index check, not the filesystem, is what decides, so an untracked file never validates an address. Opposite direction: on the clean tree the grader reports zero defects across 80 files and 155 distinct addresses, so no live address a reader could follow is reported dead.

every_registered_check_actually_runs.detail: Measured from the transcript, not the import list. 57 checks registered across the five groups; 69 '== ' headers executed, the extra 12 being tooling shard sub-headers. Per group, not_executed = 0 for STALENESS (4, folded into REPOSITORY_CHECKS rather than spliced separately), REPOSITORY (44 including staleness), HARNESS (2), INTEGRITY (2), COMMISSIONING (2) and PARTICIPANT (7). The spliced table is 57 and registered-but-never-run is empty, so the merge kept both sides' registrations and the defect this branch hit once has not recurred.

the_sdlc_release_refusal_was_not_weakene.detail: Duty 4 is unchanged in scope: refuse, visibly and with a receipt, every EXTERNAL_WORLD step -- publishing, initializing remotes, enabling integrations, announcements. Only the carriers named in the refusal changed, from two identifiers to three carriers, and all three were checked live: STATUS.yaml owner_holds O1, reason PUBLICATION, blocks repository.publish_public; PUBLICATION.md exists; contracts/acceptance-policy.json hold_reasons contains PUBLICATION. The replacement sentence about engineering proceeding under the working name is STATUS.yaml's own reachable_alternative text. The refusal is now anchored to records that exist, which the previous wording was not.

the_volatile_and_retired_kinds_are_limit.detail: check_volatile and check_retired both iterate the entries of contracts/harness-claims.json and match nothing else, so the code does exactly what the contract's 'declared' section says, and the contract states the limitation plainly: a new way of writing 'this service is not built yet' is not caught until it is added there. Nothing claimed as derived is a hand-list: CAPABILITY is an allow-list rule over contracts/harness-hosts.json that refuses any tool outside it, named or not; REFERENCE derives from git's index over four declared roots; STANDING derives from every <subject>_status line in STATUS.yaml, read line by line so the eight legitimately doubled keys are not collapsed. The eight doubled keys reproduce exactly against lint's own WARN list.

the_contract_describes_its_own_reach_acc.detail: It does not, and this is the finding that most matters because the file exists to stop a green run being read as an assurance nobody gave. Its summary reads 'Two of the five claim kinds are derived from records and generalize; two are declared vocabulary and one is a presence check' -- but the same file documents SIX kinds, and THREE of them under derived (CAPABILITY, REFERENCE, STANDING). The module docstring repeats the error, saying 'Two kinds are derived' and then naming three. main() prints 'six kinds' and ALL_CHECKS holds six functions. The per-kind descriptions underneath are individually accurate; it is the self-count that is wrong. Recorded as F1.

the_known_drift_disclosure_is_accurate.detail: The exemption is defensible; the count describing it is not. contracts/harness-claims.json known_drift says PUBLIC-CLEARANCE is 'still cited in eight workflow prompts and three skills', and commit 99b7942 repeats 'eight workflow prompts'. Independently counted at this head: NINE workflow files, one occurrence each, every one inside a prompt string; TWO skill files carrying three occurrences between them; and .claude/README.md, which the disclosure does not mention at all. Twelve files, fourteen occurrences. Recorded as F2.

the_cold_start_corpus_note_is_honest_abo.detail: It is, and unusually so. The note now says the host section records one workstation's facts, that most of its questions carry no probe, that it therefore cannot detect its own drift and did not catch the PowerShell assumption that reached four agent definitions, and -- the part that makes it honest rather than merely candid -- that A36 and A37 grade repository declarations instead and 'are not a fix for that section'. It claims no repair it did not make. Two qualifications are carried as F6 and F7 rather than as failures of this predicate.

findings: F1 OPEN, MEDIUM, INSIDE THIS CONCERN. contracts/harness-claims.json miscounts its own reach: 'Two of the five claim kinds are derived' where the file documents six kinds and three derived. scripts/sov_harness.py's module docstring carries the same error. A contract whose stated purpose is that 'a grader that overstates its reach is worse than an absent one' should not understate its own by one kind and its derived set by one. The per-kind text is correct; only the tally is wrong, so the repair is two sentences.

F2 OPEN, MEDIUM, INSIDE THIS CONCERN. The PUBLIC-CLEARANCE known_drift entry undercounts and is incomplete: 'eight workflow prompts and three skills' against an observed nine workflow files, two skill files (three occurrences), and .claude/README.md unmentioned. Commit 99b7942 repeats 'eight'. This is precisely the class of hand-written count that main's own 'counted populations' check exists to grade in live prose, and contract JSON is outside that check's reach, so nothing would ever have caught it.

F3 OPEN, LOW, DEFENSIBLE AS SCOPED. PUBLIC-CLEARANCE and no_external_effects_in_phase_i are both absent from STATUS.yaml -- verified by grep, neither resolves. One is enforced as RETIRED and the other exempted as 'drift rather than falsehood'. No record supplies that distinction; the operative reason is the one the contract itself gives, that enforcing it would fail the build on text this branch is not repairing. Judged: leaving it is defensible because the limit is declared in the contract rather than hidden behind a green run, and the follow_up names the repair. It does not make the grader misleading. What does undercut the disclosure is F2, since a reader sizing the residual is given the wrong number.

F4 OPEN, MEDIUM, 6a -- THE CHECK'S OWN INPUTS. Both new HARNESS_CHECKS declare observes tuples that omit files they genuinely read. 'harness claims' declares CLAUDE.md, STATUS.yaml, contracts/harness-hosts.json and scripts/sov_harness.py, but check_volatile and check_retired read contracts/harness-claims.json for their entire vocabulary. 'harness claim refusals fire' declares only scripts/sov_harness.py, but executes scripts/sovharness/fixtures.py and copies both contracts. Nothing grades an observes tuple against what its check actually reads -- scripts/sovland/isolation.py documents this as its own known blind spot and says the whole of its defence is that paragraph -- and test_verify_observations.py asserts only that the tuple is non-empty and its paths exist. So a change confined to contracts/harness-claims.json that broke the harness check would produce a failure whose declared addresses do not contain the changed file, which is the exact input to landing attribution that module names as undetectable. This witness did not determine which way attribution would then err; the point is that it cannot be determined from the record.

F5 OPEN, LOW, DECLARED. REFERENCE resolves an address from any service root, so `contracts/service.json` validates via services/*/contracts/service.json even though no repository-root contracts/service.json exists -- confirmed by probe, exit 0. An address a reader standing at the root cannot follow therefore passes. This is declared in the contract's REFERENCE description, so it is a disclosed looseness rather than a misrepresentation, and it is the price of not reporting eighteen live addresses as dead.

F6 OPEN, LOW, 6a. Cold-start A36 asks which tool names an agent definition may declare and grades set_eq against contracts/harness-hosts.json 'portable' -- the same file that is the answer. It pins the declaration against silent change, which has value, but it measures nothing about any host and cannot detect the inverse error of a tool declared portable that no invocation provides. Disclosed rather than hidden: harness-hosts.json says 'Declaring a tool here does not grant it', and the corpus note says A36/A37 are not a fix for the host section.

F7 OPEN, LOW, 6a. Cold-start A37 grades a capability fact by regex over one CLAUDE.md sentence's exact phrasing, '^- Shell: use the `(\w+)` tool'. That is prose wording standing in for the fact. It is not hypothetical: commits 2a373e4 and da4b101 on this very branch carry the wording '- Shell: reached through the `Bash` tool, on every platform this repository is worked on', which does not match the pattern, so the probe passes at the tip only because the final commit reworded the line back. A benign edit to that sentence breaks the probe without changing anything it purports to grade.

F8 OPEN, LOW, PHRASING. Commit da4b101 says 'Two coldstart probes cover the failure class'. Nothing executes them in the build: scripts/sov_coldstart.py is in neither the verify check table nor .github/, and the 'semantic cold-start task' check in verify runs six custody checks that never read corpus.json. Run by hand both probes resolve and match (A36 returns the fifteen portable tools, A37 returns 'Bash'), so the claim is true as recorded-in-the-corpus and overstated as covered. The real gate for this failure class is check_capability, which does run inside verify.
residuals: The subject moved twice under this witness, 0f65d90 -> 937f833 -> 99b7942, and the middle state silently dropped the repair. Both earlier readings are superseded; nothing from them is carried by assertion, and every predicate above was re-measured at 99b7942. CLAUDE.md trap T6 is the standing hazard and it fired here.

No GitHub check-run state was observed. gh is not installed on this host, so the reported '16 check runs, 15 success, 1 skipped' at 99b7942 is neither confirmed nor disputed by this record. Trap T5 is directly on point: a skipped required check satisfies the ruleset without running, and this witness cannot say which check was skipped or whether it was required. Treat that line as unattested.

verify exit 0 is not conformance (trap T2). It reports 'PASS: 57 checks' and simultaneously records no wall-clock grade at 15.381s and 9 checks over their budget ceilings; both are attributed debt under contracts/verification-budget.json and neither refuses. The many FAIL: lines inside the transcript are declared negative controls inside passing checks, not failures of this run.

The grader reads only backticked addresses, only the sentence form '<subject>_status is <TOKEN>', and only the listed vocabulary for VOLATILE and RETIRED. Each limit is declared in contracts/harness-claims.json. Silence from this grader over any other prose is coverage boundary, not confirmation.
PROVENANCE is presence-only by design and recomputes no digest; the contract names verifying it a DEPENDENCY_SEAM. A vendored skill whose declared fields are all present but wrong passes.
Nothing grades contracts/harness-claims.json itself. It has no schema, is in no fixture census, and is validated by no check -- which is how F1's miscount and F2's wrong counts reached a green build.

This record conforms to contracts/participant-observation.schema.json, which the landing gate is recorded as refusing for want of a top-level CONFIRMED verdict the schema forbids (OPEN-SEAMS.md S29). This witness did not add the forbidden fields and does not settle that conflict.

Not settled here: whether the change may land; whether any claim outside the grader's declared reach is true; whether the eleven remaining PUBLIC-CLEARANCE citations should be repaired now; any service, requirement or phase standing.
judgement_items: None of the eight findings is judgement-typed. F1, F2, F4 and F8 are text and declaration repairs inside this concern and belong to the builder under AGENTS.md Closure ownership; F3, F5, F6 and F7 are disclosed limits recorded so a reader sizes the green run correctly. Filing any of them as a new ticket would move the defect out of the concern that owns it.
